questions.q: When Lot saw the two angels coming into Sodom, what did he offer to them?
questions.a: Lot offered that they stay at his home for the night and then leave in the morning.

questions.q: What was the angels’ response to Lot?
questions.a: The angels said that they would spend the night in the street.

questions.q: At Lot’s strong urging, where did the angels finally decide to spend the night?
questions.a: Finally, the angels went with Lot to his home for the night.

questions.q: What did the men of the city who surrounded Lot’s house want Lot to do?
questions.a: The men wanted Lot to bring out the two men who were visiting him, so they could know then carnally.

questions.q: What did Lot offer the men of the city instead?
questions.a: Lot offered the men of the city his two daughters instead of the two visitors.

questions.q: How did the men respond to Lot’s offer?
questions.a: The men told Lot to stand back, and they almost broke down the door.

questions.q: What did the angels then do?
questions.a: The angels pulled Lot back into the house and struck the men outside with blindness.

questions.q: What did the angels say they had been sent to do by Yahweh?
questions.a: The angels said they had been sent to destroy the city.

questions.q: How did Lot’s sons-in-law respond when Lot told them to hurry and leave Sodom because it was about to be destroyed?
questions.a: Lot’s sons-in-law thought Lot was joking.

questions.q: When morning dawned, what did the angels tell Lot to do?
questions.a: The angels told Lot to take his wife and daughters and get out of the city so they would not be destroyed too.

questions.q: Why, despite Lot’s lingering, did the angels bring Lot and his family by their hands out of the city?
questions.a: The angels set them outside the city because Yahweh was merciful to them.

questions.q: What instructions did the angels give Lot when they were outside the city?
questions.a: The angels told Lot and his family to flee for their lives and to not look back.

questions.q: Where did the angel allow Lot and his family to flee?
questions.a: Lot and his family were allowed to flee to a small city called Zoar.

questions.q: What did Yahweh do when Lot reached Zoar?
questions.a: Yahweh rained down sulfur and fire from the sky on Sodom and Gomorrah.

questions.q: What did Lot’s wife do, and what happened to her?
questions.a: Lot’s wife looked back, and she became a pillar of salt.

questions.q: What did Abraham see early in the morning as he looked down at all the land of the plain?
questions.a: Abraham saw smoke rising from the land like the smoke of a furnace.

questions.q: To where did Lot then move and why?
questions.a: Lot then moved to a cave in the mountains, because he was afraid to live in Zoar.

questions.q: What plan did Lot’s daughters make involving their father?
questions.a: Lot’s daughters planned to make their father drunk, then lie with him so that they could have children.

questions.q: Which two people groups came from the daughters of Lot?
questions.a: The Moabite and Ammonite people groups came from the daughters of Lot.

commentary.text: The destruction of Sodom, and the deliverance of Lot.
The sin and disgrace of Lot.

Verses 1–29 Lot was good, but there was not one more of the same character in the city. All the people of Sodom were very wicked and vile. Care was therefore taken for saving Lot and his family. Lot lingered; he trifled. Thus many who are under convictions about their spiritual state, and the necessity of a change, defer that needful work. The salvation of the most righteous men is of God's mercy, not by their own merit. We are saved by grace. God's power also must be acknowledged in bringing souls out of a sinful state If God had not been merciful to us, our lingering had been our ruin. Lot must flee for his life. He must not hanker after Sodom. Such commands as these are given to those who, through grace, are delivered out of a sinful state and condition. Return not to sin and Satan. Rest not in self and the world. Reach toward Christ and heaven, for that is escaping to the mountain, short of which we must not stop. Concerning this destruction, observe that it is a revelation of the wrath of God against sin and sinners of all ages. Let us learn from hence the evil of sin, and its hurtful nature; it leads to ruin.

See the peril of security. Lot, who kept chaste in Sodom, and was a mourner for the wickedness of the place, and a witness against it, when in the mountain, alone, and, as he thought, out of the way of temptation, is shamefully overtaken. Let him that thinks he stands high, and stands firm, take heed lest he fall. See the peril of drunkenness; it is not only a great sin itself, but lets in many sins, which bring a lasting wound and dishonour. Many a man does that, when he is drunk, which, when he is sober, he could not think of without horror. See also the peril of temptation, even from relations and friends, whom we love and esteem, and expect kindness from. We must dread a snare, wherever we are, and be always upon our guard. No excuse can be made for the daughters, nor for Lot. Scarcely any account can be given of the affair but this, The heart is deceitful above all things, and desperately wicked: who can know it? From the silence of the Scripture concerning Lot henceforward, learn that drunkenness, as it makes men forgetful, so it makes them to be forgotten.
